questions.stem: For n=15, what is the critical number of positive signs for a two-sided sign test at alpha approximately 0.05?
questions.explanation: With n=15, reject if positives <=3 or >=12 (two-sided p≈0.035+0.035). The low critical count is 3.
questions.hint: Find the binomial tail for n=15.

questions.stem: What is a common tradeoff of distribution-free tests?

options.text: They may have less power than parametric tests when assumptions hold

questions.explanation: Distribution-free tests can have less power when parametric assumptions hold. They are not invalid.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.topic: Exact sign-test p-value from a count
questions.learningObjective: Compute an exact sign-test p-value
questions.stem: In a sign test with 13 non-tied observations, 11 are positive; what is the two-sided exact p-value?
questions.explanation: 2 times P(X>=11) under Binomial(13,0.5) = 2*(78+13+1)/8192 = 0.02246. Normal approximation would differ.
questions.hint: Use the binomial with n=13, p=0.5.

questions.topic: Exact sign-test p-value and its reading
questions.learningObjective: Explain the difference between one- and two-sided p-values
questions.stem: How does a one-sided p-value compare to a two-sided p-value for the same data?

options.text: It is double the two-sided p-value
It is half the two-sided p-value when the direction matches

questions.explanation: When the observed direction matches, the one-sided p-value is half the two-sided. They are not always equal.
